_doc: The DELIBERATE-REMOVAL ledger for `npm run api:check` (R3-261).
The SDK's public API is additive-only (SDK_PACKAGING_SPEC §9) so a pinned or
forked app keeps compiling (UI_AS_APPS §0/§7, core value #4). The gate compares
the SHAPE of every export against api-snapshot.json, so removing an export, an
interface field, a union member or a parameter all fail it.
A gate with no legitimate way to retire something gets deleted the first time
someone genuinely needs to retire something. This file is that way: an entry
here makes one specific removal allowed, and `npm run api:update` REFUSES to
write a snapshot that drops anything not listed, so re-running the updater is
not a way past the gate. A deliberate break therefore lands in two reviewed
diffs — this ledger (with the reason) and the snapshot.
Each entry needs all four fields; `detail` is copied verbatim from the failure
message (`api:check` prints the exact entry to paste):
module  the api-snapshot.json module key, e.g. "mounts"
export  the exported name, e.g. "Member"
detail  what is lost — "the export itself", "member `principal?`",
"union member `'reader'`", "now requires 2 parameters (was 1)", …
reason  WHY this is deliberate, and what consumers should use instead.
A removal without a stated reason is not a documented removal.
Entries are permanent history: they stay after the snapshot is regenerated, so
the record of what was retired, when and why survives.

removals.reason: R3-546 bumps the @immediately-run/mdx-plugins pin 0.5.0 → 0.7.1 (the SDK re-exports LinkSpace from it), which propagates mdx-plugins' own R3-482 rename window: `corpusRoot: string | null` becomes optional and the canonical `bundleRoot?: string | null` arrives beside it, read new-then-old by the resolver. NOT a runtime break: link resolution is dual-read (a caller spelling either field resolves identically — the window `cross_repo_migration` prescribes), and the optionality flip is the checker's name for the rename. A strict reader of `corpusRoot` now sees `string | null | undefined`; use `bundleRoot`, or null-check. The alternative — not bumping — would fork the bundle-layout vocabulary this SDK minor exists to carry (`SandboxMount.bundle`).

R3-482 corpus→bundle symbol rename. NOT a consumer-visible break: `CorpusScope` is still exported, now as a type alias of `BundleScope`, so `Context<CorpusScope>` and `Context<BundleScope>` are the SAME type and a pinned consumer's annotation still compiles (verified under `strict` against the built dist with every old spelling, including this exact annotation). `CorpusContext` itself is a re-export of `BundleContext` — one object, two spellings, pinned by src/corpus.test.ts — so React context identity holds for an app mid-migration. The gate compares the type's NAME, which is what changed. Use `BundleScope`.

R3-876 review round 1 (both passes, R6): the hand-written UrlChangeMessage interface duplicated UrlchangePayload, which the pinned @immediately-run/sandbox-protocol@0.17.0 already exports; the sites now import the contract's own type. NEVER SHIPPED: the interface existed only on the PR branch between its first commit and this fix — no release carried it (0.79.0 predates it; 0.80.0 publishes without it), so no consumer could pin it.

R3-984: not a removal — the error member GAINED two optional fields (recovery?, openPR?), and the snapshot names a union member by its full key set, so the widened member reads as `{message, recoverable, stage}` lost plus `{message, openPR?, recoverable, recovery?, stage}` added. Every value of the old member is still a value of the new one; a pinned consumer keeps compiling.
